title: Model Capacity
text:
Model Capacity
What Can Linear Regression Learn?
Key Message
• Linear regression is a linear function approximator.
• Prediction is always an affine function of the input:
ˆy = w Tx + b
Linear regression cannot model non-linear target functions in the original input space.

title: Model Capacity
text:
Model Capacity
Geometric Interpretation
Function Space View
• Linear regression fits a function in a linear hypothesis space.
• For 1D input: predicted curve is always a straight line.
• For higher dimensions: prediction is a hyperplane.
Model capacity is limited by the dimensionality and linearity of the feature space.

title: Model Capacity
text:
Model Capacity
Implications
Limitations
• Cannot represent:
• Curved functions (e.g. sin x, x2)
• Periodic patterns
• Piecewise or highly non-linear relationships
The limitation comes from the linear form, not from the loss function.
Key Idea
• Linear regression is always linear in the feature space.
• Next: we need feature transformation.

title: Model Capacity
text:
Model Capacity
What Can Softmax Regression Learn?
Implications
• Class regions are convex polytopes
• Boundaries are combinations of hyperplanes
• Cannot represent curved or disconnected class regions
Softmax regression generalizes logistic regression to multi-class settings, but remains linear
in feature space.
Key Idea
• Logistic / Softmax regression are always linear
• Next: we need feature transformation

title: Overfitting vs Underfitting
text:
Overfitting vs Underfitting
Intuition
Underfitting
Model is too simple; cannot capture the true pattern in the data.
• High training error and high validation error
• Example: linear model for a curved relationship
Overfitting
Model is too complex; memorizes training data including noise.
• Low training error but high validation error
• Example: high-degree polynomial that wiggles through every training
point
Goal
Find a model complexity that balances both: good generalization to unseen
data.

text:
Feature Transformation
Why Linear Models Fail on Nonlinear Patterns
A Linear Model is Always Linear in Its Inputs
ˆy = w Tx + b
⇒
hyperplane decision boundary / straight-line regression
The Bottleneck
• The limitation is not the optimizer, not the dataset size.
• The limitation is the hypothesis class: linear functions in the current
feature space.
To learn nonlinear relations, we must change the feature space.

title: Feature Transformation
text:
Feature Transformation
The Core Trick: Linear in Φ(x)
Feature Mapping
Define a mapping:
Φ : RD →RM
Then apply a linear model:
ˆy = w TΦ(x) + b
Interpretation
• The model is still linear in parameters (w, b).
• But it can be nonlinear in the original input x.
This is the foundation of basis expansion, kernels, and deep networks.

title: Feature Transformation
text:
Feature Transformation
Three Families of Feature Transformations
1) Manual Feature Transform
• Polynomial features, Fourier basis
• RBF features, kernels (implicit Φ)
2) Shallow Learned Features
• MLP: (FC + Nonlinearity)+ as Φ
3) Deep Learned Features
• CNN (2012), RNN, GNN
• Transformer (2017), Mamba (2023–)

title: Representation Learning
text:
Representation Learning
Historical Perspective
Before Deep Learning
• Humans design features manually
• Examples:
• Polynomial features
• SIFT, HOG
• Domain-specific descriptors
With Deep Learning
• Features are learned automatically from data
• Neural networks learn Φ directly
Deep learning replaces manual feature engineering with learned
representations.

Connection to Deep Learning
Key Observation
• Deep networks = many stacked transformations
Φ(x) = fL(· · · f2(f1(x)))

Interpretation

Deep learning = deep representation learning.
